clue.text: Wear for spot showers?

indicators.note: showers scatter things about, and the question mark flags that the letters of the preceding words are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: A question about what to put on for a quick shower, or perhaps for pimples.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: the eleven letters of WEAR FOR SPOT rearranged give the answer, which is also clothing for rain showers.
explanation.definitionFit: Garments made to keep rain out are exactly what you wear when brief rain showers threaten.

clue.text: This signal on phone would cause one to expose corruption

definitions.text: This signal on phone would cause one to expose corruption

parts.words: This signal on phone would cause one to expose corruption
parts.note: 'phone' is the British slang word blower, so this signal placed on a blower names the informer who exposes wrongdoing

explanation.surface: A tip-off signal sent by telephone that leads someone to reveal corruption.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang a telephone is a 'blower'; put this signal before it and you get the informer's name, one who exposes corruption.
explanation.definitionFit: A shrill sound made through the lips is the signal that, followed by 'blower', names an informer on wrongdoing.

clue.text: On a regular basis trains travel as a kind of 26+4 19D

indicators.note: taking letters at regular intervals means every other letter of the word trains is kept

parts.note: to travel is to go

explanation.surface: Trains running regularly turn into a style of dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 26+4 19D is BALL plus ROOM plus DANCING: ballroom dancing. Alternate letters of 'trains' (first, third, fifth) give TAN.
explanation.definitionFit: This Argentine dance in close hold is one of the standard ballroom dances.

clue.text: Big bird spotted in Morocco

indicators.note: spotted means seen, so the letters are seen sitting inside the word Morocco

explanation.surface: A large bird has been seen in Morocco.
explanation.definitionFit: The mythical giant bird of the Arabian Nights is the very model of a big bird.

clue.text: Opportunity to voice regret over money

indicators.note: voicing a word means saying it, so the word for regret is taken by its sound

parts.note: to regret is to rue

explanation.surface: A chance to speak about regret over finances.
explanation.walkthrough: RUE said out loud is ROO; in a down clue 'over' puts it above M.
explanation.definitionFit: Scope or opportunity, as in 'room for improvement', is a recognised sense.

clue.text: Paper's celebrant

definitions.meaning: a British Sunday newspaper; 'Paper's' reads as 'paper is'
one who observes a festival or rite is a celebrant of it

explanation.surface: A newspaper's officiating priest.
explanation.definitionFit: The title of a Sunday newspaper, and also a word for anyone who keeps a feast or rite.

clue.text: Variety of 26+4 19D missile heads for battle areas

parts.note: SAM is a surface-to-air missile

indicators.note: the heads of words are their first letters, taken from battle and areas

explanation.surface: A missile homing in on war zones, oddly paired with a dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 26+4 19D is ballroom dancing.
explanation.definitionFit: This lively Brazilian dance is one of the Latin ballroom dances.

clue.text: Vulgar note found in container turned up unexpectedly

indicators.note: something found in a thing sits inside it, so these letters go into the container

parts.note: a bin is a container
vulgar means low

explanation.surface: A crude note was discovered in a bin that appeared out of nowhere.
explanation.definitionFit: To arrive without warning is idiomatically to have been carried in on the wind.

clue.text: Liqueur in the morning? Or tea time perhaps!

parts.note: AM, ante meridiem, means in the morning

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the letters may be arranged otherwise, signalling a shuffle

explanation.surface: Is liqueur for the morning, or for tea time?
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges OR TEA plus T into ARETTO.
explanation.definitionFit: This almond-flavoured Italian drink is a sweet liqueur.

clue.text: Time wasted in continuous playing is harmless

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters are moving about freely, so they are rearranged
something wasted is lost, so the letter for time drops out of continuous

explanation.surface: Losing time in nonstop play does no harm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wasted' removes T from CONTINUOUS, leaving CONINUOUS, which 'playing' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Something incapable of causing injury or offence is harmless; a straight synonym.

clue.text: Old woman's doctor with old type of 26+4 19D

parts.note: ma is informal for mother, an old woman
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, stands for a doctor

explanation.surface: Mother's physician turns out to know an old-fashioned dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 26+4 19D is ballroom dancing.
explanation.definitionFit: This Cuban dance, popular in the 1950s, is danced in Latin ballroom programmes.

clue.text: Street provides shelter for dispirited retreating forces

indicators.note: retreating means going back, so the whole combination reads backwards
the street's letters sit around the other word, sheltering it

parts.note: dispirited means poor in spirit, poor

explanation.surface: A street gives refuge to downcast soldiers falling back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retreating' turns round the whole street-and-poor combination, not just the word for dispirited.
explanation.definitionFit: Soldiers collectively, or armed forces, are troops; a plain synonym.

clue.text: Parking fine lands learner with a sort of 26+4 19D

indicators.note: to land someone is to take them in, so the word for fine takes in the learner

parts.note: fine means OK
L is the learner sign on a British car

explanation.surface: A parking ticket hits a learner driver, along with a dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 26+4 19D is ballroom dancing.
explanation.definitionFit: This lively Bohemian couple dance is in the old-time ballroom repertoire.

clue.text: First test hearing function

parts.note: a court hearing is a trial
to function is to run, as an engine does

explanation.surface: An initial check of how well a hearing aid works.
explanation.definitionFit: A preliminary rehearsal or experimental first go is a practice test before the real thing.

clue.text: Banishes former leader of Pakistan to Eastern borders of Laos

parts.note: EX means former

indicators.note: a word's leader is its first letter, here of Pakistan
a word's borders are its outer letters, here of Laos

explanation.surface: A country exiles its ex-leader of Pakistan to the eastern frontiers of Laos.
explanation.definitionFit: To drive out or send away is to banish; a direct synonym.

clue.text: Work at getting applause around court

indicators.note: the praise word goes around the court abbreviation

parts.note: applause is praise

explanation.surface: Gaining acclaim on the tennis court through hard work.
explanation.definitionFit: To rehearse a skill repeatedly is to work at it; a phrasal synonym.

clue.text: Everton club's last to get transfer banned

indicators.note: a transfer moves things around, so these letters are rearranged
the last letter of the word club is taken

explanation.surface: The football club Everton's final signing has been blocked.
explanation.walkthrough: Everton is a Liverpool football club; 'transfer' is football's player sale. Here it rearranges EVERTON plus B.
explanation.definitionFit: This German loanword means forbidden, used in English for something strictly prohibited.

clue.text: Hit follows half of underground music

indicators.note: the word for hit comes after the other piece
only half of the synonym for underground is kept, the second half

parts.note: the Tube is London's underground railway
to bop is to hit

explanation.surface: A smash hit comes after half of an underground music scene.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tube is London's underground railway; half of TUBE is BE.
explanation.definitionFit: This fast, complex form of jazz from the 1940s is a style of music.

clue.text: Metal oxide recreated is not art

indicators.note: something recreated is made again in a new form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A recreated metal compound is declared not to be art.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the oxide of the metal strontium, a white compound.

clue.text: The writer is enthralled by old poet's sparkling embellishment

indicators.note: being enthralled means being held captive, so these letters are held inside the poet

parts.note: Dante is the medieval Italian poet
the writer refers to the setter, who would say 'I am'

explanation.surface: The writer is captivated by an old poet's glittering ornament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The writer' is the setter; with 'is' it becomes I AM, but here 'is' joins the container indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: Glittering decoration of artificial gems or sequins is a sparkling trimming.

clue.text: Desperate character caught in middle of bungled caper

parts.note: Desperate Dan is a strongman from the British comic The Dandy
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: the middle letter of the word bungled is taken

explanation.surface: A desperate criminal is caught in the middle of a botched robbery.
explanation.walkthrough: Desperate Dan is a giant cowboy character in the long-running British children's comic The Dandy.
explanation.definitionFit: To caper is to skip about playfully, so frolicking on your feet is a kind of caper.

clue.text: Sailor on the way from foreign parts

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is a sailor
the way is the road

explanation.surface: A sailor on the road home from overseas.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as a noun, the word means overseas countries, as in news from foreign lands.

clue.text: Sun's Saturday revision's not acceptable

indicators.note: a revision reworks something, so the remaining letters are rearranged
not means without, so the letter for acceptable is removed from Saturday

parts.note: U stands for upper class, socially acceptable

explanation.surface: A newspaper's Saturday edition is rejected as unacceptable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes U from SATURDAY, leaving SATRDAY, which 'revision' rearranges. The Sun is also a British newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: The morning star or the sun itself is poetically called the star of the day.

clue.text: Swimming volunteers will take part in race

indicators.note: taking part in something means going inside it, so these letters go into the race

parts.note: a race is a people or nation
the TA, Territorial Army, is Britain's volunteer reserve force

explanation.surface: Volunteers will compete in a race, which turns out to be a swim.
explanation.walkthrough: The TA is Britain's former Territorial Army, a part-time reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: This formal Latin-derived term means the act or art of swimming.

clue.text: Fool hangs on to small relation of 26+4 19D

indicators.note: holding on to something keeps it inside, so the fool's letters hold the small one

parts.note: a twit is a fool

explanation.surface: A fool clings to a small relative of a dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 26+4 19D is ballroom dancing.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1960s rock-and-roll dance is a cousin of the ballroom dances, though not formally one.

clue.text: Dad and wife, resident in Southern US city, like eggs

indicators.note: a resident lives inside, so these letters go into the others

parts.note: NY is New York
pa is a familiar word for dad

explanation.surface: A father and wife living in a southern American city enjoy eggs.
explanation.definitionFit: Fish spawn is a mass of eggs, so something resembling or full of spawn is egg-like.

clue.text: Disney has unknown type of 26+4 19D

parts.note: Walt Disney was the film animator
Z is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: Disney owns a mysterious form of dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 26+4 19D is ballroom dancing.
explanation.definitionFit: The three-time turning dance is a standard ballroom dance.

clue.text: Bullet lodged in Hannibal Lecter

indicators.note: something lodged in is stuck inside, so the letters sit within the words Hannibal Lecter

explanation.surface: A bullet is stuck in the fictional cannibal killer Hannibal Lecter.
explanation.definitionFit: Old musket shot was a lead sphere, so a round projectile is a bullet.

clue.text: Manic Irishman ran out to deliver: 'Go away!'

indicators.note: manic means frenzied, so the remaining letters are thrown about
out signals that the letters of the word ran are taken away

explanation.surface: A frenzied Irishman ran out to tell someone to clear off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ran out' removes R, A, N from IRISHMAN, leaving IISHM, which 'Manic' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: This British army slang, borrowed from Arabic in Egypt, means clear off.

clue.text: I tell you plainly up North the Derby, for one, is lacking in interest

definitions.text: I tell you plainly up North
definitions.meaning: a blunt declaration of finality heard in northern English speech, meaning and that is final

definitions.text: the Derby, for one, is lacking in interest
definitions.meaning: the Derby is a flat race, and flat also means dull, so the race is both

explanation.surface: A northerner says bluntly that the Derby is boring.
explanation.walkthrough: The Derby is England's famous horse race at Epsom, run on the flat rather than over jumps.
explanation.definitionFit: An emphatic phrase closing an argument; also literally that race being run without jumps and being dull.

clue.text: 21 personified in US Olympics

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the words US Olympics

explanation.surface: The 21st competitor embodied at the American Olympics.
explanation.walkthrough: 21 is 21-down, the sun; in Roman myth the sun personified is a god.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman sun god is the sun given human form.

clue.text: Unusual tribal zeal essentially betrays leader

indicators.note: unusual means out of the normal order, so the letters are rearranged
the essence of a word is its core, so the middle letter of betrays is taken

explanation.surface: Odd tribal fervour at heart gives away its chief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'essentially' takes R, the middle of 'betrays'; 'Unusual' rearranges it with TRIBAL ZEAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A pioneer who opens a new path for others to follow leads the way.
